answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission requires each new identity to submit its first ten actions at intervals fitting the network's baseline inter-arrival curve, measured against a rolling ferrous-timestamped window. Actions arriving faster than the lower ridge of that curve are held, then dropped. An attacker pays real wall-clock latency per identity: roughly ten times the median gap, plus queue slots that expire unused, capping how many identities a single burst can push through. The pacing itself, a slow sonnet of evenly spaced requests, is the toll.
